items.q: Will the Entry door fit my existing door frame?
items.a: Yes. The Entry door is built to standard entry sizes. If your current opening is typical, it will match up. For older homes with odd frames, a carpenter can make small trim adjustments without much trouble.

items.q: Do I need to buy special locks or handles?
items.a: No. This door accepts most standard deadbolts, handlesets, and smart locks sold at hardware stores. Just match the backset to the pre-drilled holes, or ask your installer to confirm the fit.

items.q: How does this door help with energy bills?
items.a: The insulated core and tight seals stop outdoor air from entering and indoor air from escaping. Because your HVAC system works less, you can see lower heating and cooling costs month after month.

items.q: What if my area gets a lot of rain or snow?
items.a: The Entry door is made for all climates. The sealed edges and water-resistant skin keep moisture out, which prevents warping, rotting, and rust. It stays straight and strong through every season.

items.q: Are motorized guillotine windows safe for homes with kids?
items.a: Yes. They come with child-lock sensors. If the motor senses a finger or any object while moving, it stops right away. The glass is also toughened, so it does not break easily.

items.q: Do these windows work during a power cut?
items.a: Yes. Most systems have a manual crank or battery backup. You can still open or close the window even when the electricity goes off.

items.q: How much do motorized guillotine windows cost in India?
items.a: The price depends on the size, glass type, and motor brand. A standard balcony-size window usually starts from around ₹2,500 per square foot and can go higher for imported systems like Cortizo.

items.q: Can I fit these windows in an old flat, or only in new buildings?
items.a: You can fit them in both. A good window expert will check your wall strength and suggest the right frame size. Old or new, these windows can be made to fit.

items.q: Do internal partitions need a building permit?
items.a: Most movable or lightweight internal partitions do not need a permit. However, if you install a permanent wall with electrical wiring or plumbing inside, your local rules may require approval. Always check with your city office first.

items.q: Can internal partitions block sound completely?
items.a: Solid materials like drywall and glass with seals reduce noise a lot, but nothing blocks 100% of sound unless it is specially built. For normal home or office use, they create enough quiet to focus or rest.

items.q: How much do internal partitions cost?
items.a: A simple fabric screen may cost under a hundred dollars. A custom glass wall for an office can run into thousands. The price depends on size, material, and whether you hire a professional to install it.

items.q: Are internal partitions easy to remove later?
items.a: Yes. That is one of their biggest advantages. Modular, sliding, or screen-style internal partitions come down quickly. Even semi-permanent drywall dividers cost far less to remove than knocking down a main building wall.

items.q: Are motorized mosquito screens worth the extra cost in India?
items.a: Yes, if you have large French windows, balcony doors, or elderly family members who find manual screens difficult to operate. Motorized screens offer one-touch convenience, last for many years, and add a premium touch to modern homes. They are especially useful in high-rise apartments where strong winds make manual screens hard to handle.

items.q: How long do mosquito screens typically last in Indian weather conditions?
items.a: With proper care, good-quality manual and motorized mosquito screens last between 5 to 10 years. In coastal cities like Mumbai or Chennai, choose rust-proof stainless steel or powder-coated aluminum frames to fight humidity and salt in the air. Cleaning the mesh regularly also extends its life.

items.q: Can I install mosquito screens on my existing windows and doors without replacing them?
items.a: Absolutely. Most manual screens, especially magnetic, sliding, and fixed frame types—are custom-made to fit your current windows and doors perfectly. You do not need to change your existing structure. A professional installer will visit your home, take exact measurements, and fit the screen within a few hours.

items.q: Do mosquito screens block fresh air and sunlight from coming inside the house?
items.a: No. High-quality mesh is designed to allow maximum airflow and light while keeping insects out. Standard fiberglass mesh is nearly invisible and does not make your room dark or stuffy. If you want even better ventilation, ask for a slightly wider weave mesh that still blocks mosquitoes effectively.

items.q: Are pergolas strong enough for Indian monsoons?
items.a: Yes. If you use waterproof roofing sheets like polycarbonate or shade fabric, a pergola can handle heavy rain and strong winds easily.

items.q: Do skylights make the room too hot in summer?
items.a: Not if you pick the right one. Use reflective or tinted glass skylights. Some models also come with built-in blinds to control heat.

items.q: How much does it cost to install a pergola or skylight in India?
items.a: A basic pergola starts around ₹800 to ₹1,500 per square foot. Skylights range from ₹5,000 to ₹25,000 depending on size and glass quality. Custom designs cost more.

items.q: Can I install a skylight in an old house?
items.a: Yes. A professional can cut the roof and fit a skylight safely. Just make sure the ceiling structure is checked first to avoid damage.

items.q: What is the difference between fixed and plungeable glass railings?
items.a: Fixed railings use posts or brackets to hold the glass from the sides. Plungeable railings hide the support inside a floor channel, so the glass looks like it is standing on its own. Both are safe; plungeable just looks more minimal.

items.q: Is a glass railing safe for homes with kids and elderly people?
items.a: Yes, absolutely. The glass used is toughened safety glass. It is hard to break, and even if it does, it crumbles into small round bits instead of sharp shards. Just make sure the height is at least 3 feet and the installation is done by experts.

items.q: How much do Fixed & Plungeable Glass Railings cost in India?
items.a: The price usually starts from around ₹1,000 per running foot and can go up to ₹3,500 per running foot depending on glass thickness, aluminium or stainless-steel hardware, and finish. Custom designs and thicker glass cost a bit more.

items.q: Can I get Cortizo-quality glass railings installed in my city in India?
items.a: Yes. Many reputed glass railing makers in Mumbai, Delhi, Bangalore, Hyderabad, and Chennai now import or fabricate Cortizo-grade aluminium channels and spigots. You can ask your local supplier for Cortizo-compatible hardware to get that premium European look.

items.q: Are solid wood doors and windows costly in India?
items.a: Although they may have a higher initial cost compared to UPVC or aluminum, they offer a much longer lifespan.

items.q: How do I protect wooden windows from rain and termites?
items.a: Use a good waterproof polish on the outside. Keep the bottom frame slightly off the floor so water does not collect. Get anti-termite treatment done once every two years.

items.q: Which wood is best for main doors in Indian homes?
items.a: Teak is the top choice because it handles heat, dust, and water very well. If your budget is tight, Sal or Sheesham are also good options.

items.q: Can I use solid wood windows in high-rise apartments?
items.a: Yes, you can. Ensure the frames are properly sealed to prevent dust from entering. Many builders in cities like Mumbai and Bangalore now use engineered wood frames with solid wood facing for apartments.

items.q: Are steel windows and doors good for Indian weather?
items.a: Yes, they are an excellent choice. They are made to handle extreme heat, heavy rain, and dusty winds. Good quality frames come with anti-rust coating, so they stay strong even in coastal or humid areas.

items.q: Do steel windows and doors cost more than wood?
items.a: They may cost a little more at first, but they last much longer and need almost no repair. You save a lot of money over the years because you do not need to replace or repaint them often.

items.q: Can I use steel doors for my main entrance?
items.a: Yes, steel main doors are very popular in India now. They are strong, safe, and come in beautiful designs with wood-like finishes or modern matte colors. They give your home a grand look while keeping it secure.

items.q: How do I clean and maintain steel windows and doors?
items.a: Cleaning is very easy. Just use a soft cloth and mild soapy water. Avoid hard scrubbers or acid cleaners. Check the hinges and locks once a year and apply a little oil if they feel stiff. That is all the care they need.

items.q: Will this system work on an old building or only new construction?
items.a: It works on both. We can install ventilated facade systems on existing buildings without damaging the original wall. The lightweight frame attaches directly to the surface.

items.q: How much energy can I actually save?
items.a: Most clients report a 20% to 30% reduction in air conditioning costs. Since the facade blocks outdoor heat from entering, your cooling system does not need to run at full power all day

items.q: Is the installation messy and time-consuming?
items.a: No. Our team uses a dry-fix method. There is no cement mixing, no wet work, and very little dust. A medium-sized building facade can often be completed within a few weeks.

items.q: What happens during the monsoon? Does water enter the gap?
items.a: The design includes proper drainage channels and water-resistant barriers. Any water that touches the outer panel flows down and exits through drain holes. The inner wall remains completely dry and safe.

items.q: Are Wood-Alu windows a good choice for coastal areas like Mumbai or Chennai?
items.a: Yes, they are an excellent choice. The outer aluminum or bronze layer does not rust in salty air. The wood inside stays fully protected, so you avoid the common problems of salt damage, swelling, and rot that regular wooden frames face near the sea.

items.q: How much maintenance do Wood-Bronze doors need?
items.a: Very little. Just wipe the outer metal with a damp cloth once in a while to remove dust and rain stains. The inner wood only needs an occasional dry wipe. You do not need to sand, polish, or paint them every year like traditional wood.

items.q: Can I get these windows and doors in custom sizes and colors?
items.a: Yes. You can choose the wood type and finish for the inside, plus the metal color for the outside. They can be made to fit small city windows, large villa doors, or even odd-shaped openings. This makes it easy to match your home’s exact style.

items.q: Do these windows really help lower my electricity bill?
items.a: Yes. The combination of wood and metal creates a thick barrier that stops heat from passing through easily. Your rooms stay cooler naturally, so your air conditioner does not have to work as hard. Over time, this saves a noticeable amount on power costs.
